name: USB host and accessories
plain: Talks to USB devices plugged into the phone.
meaning: Reveals attached gear (drives, keyboards, radios, microcontrollers). Android lets an app drive raw USB; iPhone mostly limits apps to MFi devices and cameras.

android.permission: android.hardware.usb.host; per device USB permission dialog
android.prompt_ui: Allow app to access USB device? (with an Always open option)
android.persistence: Per device and app, optional default
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Open by default > Clear defaults
android.note: Android 14 can reset USB permission on disconnect.

ios.prompt_ui: No raw prompt; MFi chip or DriverKit entitlement
ios.note: iPhone 15 and later USB-C: UVC cameras and mics work through AVFoundation; raw USB for apps is iPadOS only.

data.update: up to 480 Mbit/s (USB 2) or 5 Gbit/s (USB 3 on supported phones)

limits.headline: Can talk to plugged in USB gear on Android; iPhone mostly limits apps to certified devices
limits.user_action: You plug in a USB device and tap Allow when asked
can: Open a connection to a drive, keyboard, radio or board (Android)
Remember your choice if you pick Always open (Android)
Use USB cameras and mics on iPhone 15 and later through the camera system
cannot: Use a device on Android without a prompt for that device
Run raw USB on iPhone; that is iPad only
Keep permission after unplug on Android 14 and later when it resets
limits.differs: Android apps can drive raw USB after a prompt; iPhone allows certified (MFi) accessories and USB cameras and mics, and raw USB only on iPad.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app talk to things plugged into the phone's USB port, like cameras, keyboards and audio gear.

marketing.name: USB host
marketing.pitch: Connect Android to USB gadgets such as keyboards, cameras and drives, and talk to them from your app.

story.for_you: You plug something in and a pop up asks whether the app may use it. On Android that can be a drive, a microphone or a gadget board. On iPhone, cameras and mics work, but most other gear does not.
story.for_makers: USB turns the phone into a tool for pros. A creator can plug in an audio interface or camera, and engineers can program boards. Android opens raw access to apps. iPhone keeps raw access for iPad.

use_cases.example: A musician plugs a studio audio interface into the phone and records a track with a recording app.
A streamer plugs in a USB camera and microphone and goes live from a phone.
A hobbyist programs a microcontroller board straight from a phone.
A gamer plugs a wired controller into a phone for console style play on the go.
A technician connects a medical or lab sensor and logs readings.
A shop plugs in a barcode scanner or card reader for the till.
A hardware security key plugged in proves who you are when you log in.

risks: Unknown gadgets can steal or inject data
story.android_note: Android 14 can reset a USB permission when the device is unplugged.
story.ios_note: iPhone 15 and later with USB-C support cameras and mics through AVFoundation. Raw USB access for apps is on iPadOS only.

technical_bounds: Vendor and product IDs expose what is plugged in

history.change: External USB-C cameras and mics for AVFoundation
